review.notes: Drafted for issue #12. Network: this drafting session could reach only en.wikipedia.org, www.wikidata.org and tiles.openfreemap.org. Refused by the proxy (CONNECT 403 or no connection): www.ibiblio.org (Ellis, Victory in the West vol. I, HyperWar transcription), archive.org and web.archive.org, www.openstreetmap.org, overpass-api.de, nominatim.openstreetmap.org, cgsc.contentdm.oclc.org (Williams 2007 thesis), apps.dtic.mil, www.ddaymuseum.co.uk (Portsmouth Museum Services FAQ), www.cwgc.org, www.iwm.org.uk, www.dday-overlord.com, www.goldbeach.org.uk, fr.wikipedia.org; history.army.mil returned HTTP 403. No official history or named historian was read directly, so every historical cite is to English Wikipedia at a pinned revision; each locator names the work the article cites (mostly Trew 2004, Ford & Zaloga 2009) so the claims can be upgraded once those or Ellis can be read. OSM: openstreetmap.org was unreachable, so OSM-derived data was read from OpenFreeMap vector tiles (planet build 20261122_124456_pt, z14). Tile feature ids are cited as seen; they appear to encode the OSM element (id×10 + 1 node / 2 way / 3 relation, e.g. 9961187072 → way/996118707), but this could not be confirmed on openstreetmap.org, so no `osm` field is set. Geometry: a single representative point on the present-day shoreline at the longitude of the Mont Fleury place node, because a 6 June 1944 aerial photograph caption (British Normandy Memorial article) places the junction of King Red and King Green in front of the Mont Fleury battery and Ver-sur-Mer. No polygon: the western limit (WN-35, Le Pont Chaussé) could not be located from a readable source, and the eastern limit at La Rivière is only implied. Open questions: Stanley Hollis's battalion is not stated in the cited sections, so it is not given. The lead says the La Rivière 88 mm gun was neutralised at 07:30; § King Sector gives no time; Normandy landings agrees on 07:30 (citing Ford & Zaloga p. 292).

summary.text: The eastern of Gold's two assault sectors, in front of Mont Fleury, Ver-sur-Mer and La Rivière. The 5th East Yorkshires and 6th Green Howards of the 69th Infantry Brigade landed first, almost together with engineers and DD tanks of the 4th/7th Dragoon Guards, which rough seas forced to be run straight onto the beach. A casemated 88 mm gun at La Rivière pinned the infantry behind the sea wall until a Westminster Dragoons flail tank fired into its embrasure. The East Yorkshires spent the morning clearing the fortified houses of La Rivière. Once a flail had cleared an exit, the Green Howards and tanks took the Mont Fleury battery and pushed on to the Meuvaines ridge and towards Crépon; the 7th Green Howards took the battery at Ver-sur-Mer. Stanley Hollis won the only Victoria Cross for D-Day in the fighting around Mont Fleury. In the second wave the 151st Brigade and the 56th Brigade, diverted from Jig, landed on King and moved inland towards the Bayeux–Caen road and Bayeux.
